definition: Personification is the tendency to understand unknown or imperfectly known phenomena in human-like terms, treating cosmic events as if they had personal qualities or agency. In this historical sense, it is linked with animism and the rise of beliefs in supernatural beings.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Demon; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports personification of cosmic phenomena as an anthropomorphic/anthropathic standpoint, but it does not explicitly support the added claim about the “rise” of beliefs in supernatural beings.
The definition slightly overextends the source by framing personification as treating phenomena as having personal agency; the packet supports human-like interpretation, not agency as such.

The definition claims that personification is “linked with … the rise of beliefs in supernatural beings,” but the packet does not support a claim about any “rise” (historical development) of such beliefs; it only states that “the personification of cosmic phenomena (animism) must be cited as the origin of all such conceptions.”
